title: MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack with enforced minimum thickness and quarter-wave initialization
scientific_hypothesis: The iteration_10 failure arose from thickness values approaching zero or negative values during optimization, triggering TMM phase singularities. Enforcing explicit minimum thickness bounds (≥20 nm) and initializing from quarter-wave optical depths centered on the 267.5 nm passband midpoint will produce physically valid candidates while maintaining the chirped dispersion strategy that achieved 0.647 target score in iteration_06.
design_principle: Alternating high/low index layers with thicknesses varying gradually across the stack to create broadband rejection outside the passband while maintaining constructive interference in the 255-280 nm transmission band.
proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
Quarter-wave optical thickness principle for bandpass filter design
expected_advantages: Enforced minimum bounds prevent TMM numerical failures
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Chirped dispersion maintains broadband rejection capability from iteration_06
known_risks: May still converge to local optima if search budget insufficient
MgF2 refractive index dispersion in deep UV may differ from nominal values
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2 (20 finite layers total). Each layer thickness bounded between 20 nm and 200 nm. Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical depth centered on 267.5 nm wavelength (MgF2 n≈1.38, HfO2 n≈2.0 at UV). Use coherent S-matrix solver across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Score three transmittance objectives: maximize mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Use bound-aware global optimizer with projection of out-of-bounds samples back into feasible region. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Iteration_10 failed with 0 valid candidates due to material_data error. This route enforces explicit minimum thickness bounds (≥20 nm) to prevent TMM phase singularities, widens thickness search interval centered on quarter-wave values, and switches to bound-aware global optimizer with projection as directed in feedback.
